steps.say: An adverb tells us more about a verb. It can tell how, when, where or how often.
An adverbial phrase is a group of words that does the same job.
steps.show: in the morning, behind the shed

steps.say: Put a comma after a phrase at the start of a sentence.
steps.show: After the storm, the sky turned gold.

check.prompt: Which word is an adverb? The boy ran quickly to school.

options.why: This is a noun. It names a place.

hints: An adverb tells about the verb.
Look for the word that answers how.
check.explanation: Quickly tells us how the boy ran.

check.prompt: Which part is an adverbial phrase? We waited at the bus stop.

options.why: This is the subject and verb.
This is only part of the phrase.
This is not a complete group.

hints: Find the group of words that answers where.
check.explanation: At the bus stop tells where we waited, so it is an adverbial phrase.
